_comment: Gate registry for claude-pipe-guard. Patterns are regular expressions matched against the HEAD of a shell segment — its command word and arguments, after leading `VAR=val` assignments and `bash`/`sudo`/`time`-style wrappers are peeled — never against the whole command string. A pattern matched against the raw string also fires on every `git show`, `grep`, and commit message that merely names the command. Anchor every pattern with `^`; the test suite enforces it. POSIX bracket classes (`[[:space:]]`) are translated to their Python equivalents, so a pattern copied from an ERE registry works unchanged. Scope: `gates` are commands whose exit status IS the answer, so losing it turns a failure into a false green — to a pipe, which yields its last stage's status, or to a backgrounded call, which yields its last statement's. Deliberately NOT every command: a registry that denies every pipeline gets overridden reflexively and then means nothing. `exempt` wins over BOTH `gates` and `mutators`, and carries the informational targets whose output, not status, is the point — including the read form of a subcommand that also has a write form (`git tag -l` beside `git tag -a`), which is the only place in the registry the two can be told apart. A capability probe (`--version`, `--help`, `-V`, `-h`) needs no entry: that shape is recognized structurally for every gate, so do not add per-tool probe patterns — they fix one tool and leave the class. `mutators` are the state-changing commands the third rule looks for AFTER a gate sequenced with `;`, where the status is read correctly and then ignored. A project extends these lists with its own `.claude/pipe-guard.json`; set `"replace": true` there to take full control instead. That file also carries `repo_state`, whose mere presence turns on the two opt-in checks that are not about exit status: a `git push` onto a base that has moved into this branch's own line ranges, and a `gh pr create` where an open PR already changes them. Nothing here ships one, so they are off by default. Every verdict is a `deny`, so the reason reaches the model rather than the user; the break-glass is a `PIPE_GUARD_OVERRIDE=<reason>` prefix on the command, and a rule that needs one routinely is a defect to fix here rather than to override.
